outcome: embolic material conversion to N-butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA)
cohort: The study population consisted of 57 women (age range, 21-43 years; mean, 32.6 years) who experienced primary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) and underwent transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) initially using gelatin sponge.
finding: Uterine height and systolic blood pressure were identified as predictive factors for embolic material conversion to N-butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) for the treatment of primary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH).
